observed.facings.png: Three panels at one scale. Each shows a row of four arching grass or grain stalks with drooping, rice-like seed heads. A thin olive ribbon runs left to right across the tops of the stalks, weaving over and under the seed heads, with a slightly tapered tip at each end. South has warm tan seed heads. East is paler and thinner-lined. North has greener, broader leaf-like heads and the ribbon's tip curls up at the right. All three are the same left-to-right composition; none shows the body end-on.
observed.south.png: Four bent stalks with tan, rice-like grain heads, standing on the bottom of the sprite. A flat olive ribbon drapes across their tops in shallow waves, with a small pointed end at the left and a hooked tip at the right. No head, eyes or face can be told apart. The stalks take up most of the opaque pixels.
observed.east.png: Almost the same picture as south: four thin, arching grass stalks with pale seed heads and a wavy ribbon laid across their tops, left to right. Thinner and lighter in colour. No head is visible.
observed.north.png: Four arching stalks with greener, broader, leaf-like seed heads and a ribbon across the top. Its right end curls upward like a tendril. Same layout as south and east. No face, but nothing marks this as the rear either.
observed.scale.png: At max zoom the candidate sits beside the human as a faint tuft of grass about one cell wide and under half the human's height. The ribbon can barely be told apart from the stalks. At 32 px per cell it is an almost invisible smudge of pale grass next to the rat.

SOUTH_FRONT.seen: South shows the ribbon lying left to right across the stalks, the same lateral layout as east. There is no head-on view and no face toward the camera.

NORTH_REAR.seen: North shows no face or eyes, though it is the same lateral layout and not a rear view of the body.

NO_OVERHEAD.seen: Every facing is a side-on view of stalks and ribbon, not an overhead view.

SAME_SIZE.seen: Measured spread 9%. The panels look about the same size.

SAME_ANIMAL.seen: The composition does not turn with the facing: south, east and north all show the same left-to-right drape over four stalks. The stalks' seed-head palette and shape also change from facing to facing (tan grain, pale grass, green leafy heads).

SIGNATURE.seen: The predator itself, a stem-thin ribbon, is barely legible. The plants dominate the sprite and the creature has no readable head or body features, so the picture reads as a clump of grain, not an animal.

ALIEN.seen: Nobody would name it as a snake; the creature hardly reads as an animal at all. The stalks look like Earth rice or wheat.

DEPARTURES.seen: 1. Flat ribbon body: present, with visible flat twists. 2. Stem-width: present, no wider than the stalks. 3. OURS.seen: Bespoke art: no vanilla or other-mod creature is recognisable.

ALPHA.seen: Four full plant stalks, from the ground up, are painted into the creature sprite. That is scenery baked into the pawn, and it will walk around with the animal.

SCALE.seen: About one cell wide and low beside the human, which fits a thin canopy predator at drawSize 1.1.

LEGIBLE.seen: At 32 px per cell it is a faint pale smudge; the ribbon cannot be seen apart from the grass.

reply.subject: RM_Ribbonwhip
reply.image_seen: facings.png shows three horizontal ribbons supported by tall stalks; south.png shows tan drooping seed heads; east.png shows paler, thinner stalks; north.png shows greener foliage leaning oppositely; scale.png shows the assembly beside a human and as a faint canopy-shaped mark at normal zoom.

concerns.evidence: All three sprites include several complete grass stalks extending from their bottom edge to the ribbon. These supporting plants occupy most of the visible assembly and are baked into the creature image.

A narrow, continuous, undulating strand visibly crosses the tops of the seed heads in each facing. Its curves follow the surrounding vegetation, matching the specified camouflage. The description does not require a conspicuous head, mouth or other predator marker; its disappearance among plants at normal zoom supports that intended identity.

south.png presents the strand stretched horizontally across four stalks, with its length exposed laterally much as in east.png. No approaching head or body receding from a front-facing end establishes the required front view.

The supporting vegetation visibly changes from tan seed heads to pale grass to green foliage. However, the ribbon itself remains a similarly coloured thin strand, and its head, underside and endpoints are insufficiently distinguishable to establish whether its anatomy turns consistently. Vegetation differences alone do not prove a change in creature anatomy.

findings.seen: Complete supporting grass stalks descend beneath the ribbon to the bottom of every sprite.
findings.quote: Real alpha: no water, rock, grass or shadow baked under the body.
findings.fix: The isolated ribbon sprite rests at canopy height over separately rendered plants, with transparent space beneath its body.

findings.seen: The ribbon's full length runs left to right across the vegetation, presenting a lateral silhouette without a readable front-facing end.
findings.quote: South = the face toward the camera.
findings.fix: The south view presents the ribbon's front end toward the camera, with its flat, stem-thin length receding across the canopy behind it.

subject: RM_Rollbug

reply.subject: RM_Rollbug

observed.facings.png: Three facings at one scale. Each shows a small, armoured, segmented isopod-like bug beside a much larger ball. The ball is packed earth bound with wire and twigs, with a skull, a ribcage, a riveted rusty metal plate and red and green cloth rags stuck in it. On south the bug faces the camera at left and the ball sits to its RIGHT, side by side. On east the bug is in profile, facing right, with its head against the ball. On north the bug's rear is in front and the ball sits behind it, up and to the right. On all three facings the ball shows nearly the same face: the skull at upper right, the ribs at centre and the plate at centre right.
observed.south.png: The bug faces the camera, with a domed, banded carapace, a small head with two dark bead eyes and short legs splayed low. The ball sits beside it on the right, not in front of it or behind it. The ball is about twice the bug's height. The background is clean alpha.
observed.east.png: A side profile of a squat isopod: overlapping armour bands, a short head and jointed legs close to the ground. Its head and forelegs push into the left side of the ball. The ball shows the skull, ribs, plate and rags. The background is clean alpha.
observed.north.png: The bug's rear: tail plates (uropods), banded back, no face or eyes. It sits low in front of the ball and overlaps its lower left. The ball sits a little higher in the frame, which makes the sprite's total height larger. The background is clean alpha.
observed.scale.png: At max zoom the rollbug (bug plus ball) is roughly a third of a cell long and well below the human's knee height. At 32 px per cell it is a tiny brown speck with a lighter round blob.

SOUTH_FRONT.seen: The bug's head and two eyes face the camera; it is a front view of the bug.

NORTH_REAR.seen: North shows the banded back and tail plates; there is no face or eyes on the bug. The skull in the ball is debris, not the creature's face.

NO_OVERHEAD.seen: All three facings are drawn from the angled game camera; none is a top-down plan.

SAME_SIZE.seen: The 18% spread comes from the ball sitting higher behind the bug on north. The bug and the ball are about the same size on every facing, so the spread is a composition effect, not a size jump.

SAME_ANIMAL.seen: The bug is consistent across facings, but the ball does not turn with it. On south the bug faces the camera and the ball sits beside it on the right, as if the east layout was kept and only the bug was rotated. A front-facing pusher should have the ball in front of it (toward the camera) or behind it. The ball also shows the same skull, ribs and plate arrangement on all three facings.

SIGNATURE.seen: A large debris ball packed with bone, scraps and metal, pushed by the bug, is the dominant shape on every facing.

ALIEN.seen: The body on its own reads as a woodlouse or pillbug. With the trash-and-bone ball, all three departures are present, so a stranger would not just name an Earth animal and stop there.

DEPARTURES.seen: 1) Present: the ball is packed debris with a skull, ribs, a riveted plate, rags and wire, not a smooth dung sphere. 2) Present: the ball is about twice the bug's height and dominates the silhouette. 3) Present: the body is low and squat and sits close to the floor; there is no head-down handstand.

STYLE.seen: Painterly, realistic texture on the armour and debris. The bead eyes on south are small and not cute. It is slightly render-like but within range.

OURS.seen: Bespoke art that matches the description; it does not resemble any vanilla or donor animal.

ALPHA.seen: Clean transparency on every facing; there is no ground patch or shadow.

SCALE.seen: Small vermin-sized creature well below the human's knee, which fits a corridor scavenger with drawSize 0.55.

LEGIBLE.seen: At 32 px per cell it reduces to a few muddy brown pixels; the bug and the ball barely separate from the floor.

findings.seen: The bug faces the camera, but the ball sits beside it on the right at the same depth, the same placement as the east profile. The ball has not moved with the bug's facing. The skull, ribs and plate are also in nearly the same arrangement on all three facings.
findings.quote: Every structure (horns, fans, sails, tails) is present and turns with the body in every view
findings.fix: On south, the bug faces the camera with the debris ball directly in front of its head, lower in the frame and partly overlapping the bug's front, so the bug reads as pushing the ball toward the viewer.

findings.seen: At 32 px per cell the rollbug is a few brown pixels; the ball and bug blur into one speck.

findings.fix: Give the ball's bone pieces a stronger light-to-dark contrast against the earth so the pale bone reads as a bold speckle at small size.

subject: RM_Shirrel

reply.subject: RM_Shirrel

observed.facings.png: Three facings at one scale. South is a narrow upright animal seen from the front: a squirrel or sugar-glider face with dark eye stripes, large rounded ears and a bushy tail fanned up behind the head. Thin tan wing membranes with jointed rods are folded down along both sides, and the four clawed feet sit at the bottom. East is a mid-glide side profile: one large bat-like wing raised high and braced by jointed spar-rods, a long bushy squirrel tail trailing behind, the forelimbs reaching forward with long hooked claws, and the head pointed with stripes and ears. North is a rear view of the same animal with two separate bat-shaped wings spread up and out, each braced by spars, ears seen from behind, no face, hind legs hanging and a big bushy tail at the bottom.
observed.south.png: Front view with the face toward the camera: a striped rodent face with dark eyes, the folded membrane and rods framing the body in a rough diamond outline, a bushy tail rising behind the head and clawed feet. Painterly with a clean outline.
observed.east.png: Side profile in flight, one bat-like wing raised with rod struts, a bushy tail trailing and a slim striped head. It reads as a flying squirrel or sugar glider with a bat wing added.
observed.north.png: Rear view with wings spread like a bat seen from behind: two separate triangular sails, each with spar struts, the back of the head and ears, no eyes, and a large bushy tail hanging down. A flight pose.
observed.scale.png: At max zoom the creature, in the east flight pose, is about as long as the human is tall and slimmer than the human. At 32 px per cell it reads as a small tan winged shape next to the rat, about twice the rat's length.

SOUTH_FRONT.seen: South shows the face head-on with both eyes and the muzzle toward the camera.

NORTH_REAR.seen: North shows the back of the head, the ears, the back, spread wings and the tail, with no face or eyes.

NO_OVERHEAD.seen: No facing is a plan view. North is a rear view, slightly from above, in a flight pose.

SAME_SIZE.seen: The 26% height spread comes from pose (wings folded on south, raised on east and north). The body and head are about the same size on all three facings.

SAME_ANIMAL.seen: Wings are folded close to the body on south but fully spread in flight on east and north. The facings show different states of the creature rather than one pose turned.

SIGNATURE.seen: The opening glide sail with spar struts is clearly visible on east and north.

ALIEN.seen: A striped sugar-glider/squirrel face, big ears and a bushy squirrel tail on every facing. A stranger would say 'a flying squirrel with bat wings' at first glance. The kite-like spars are the only alien cue.

DEPARTURES.seen: 1 ABSENT: north and east show two separate bat-like wings, not one flat diamond kite sail (only the folded south outline is roughly diamond). 2 PRESENT: stiff jointed spar rods brace the sail. 3 ABSENT: on the closed south the membrane and rods are still plainly visible along the sides. 4 PRESENT (weak): long hooked climbing claws on the forelimbs on east and south. 5 ABSENT: bushy tail and a big-eyed striped rodent head, which is the exact silhouette to avoid.

STYLE.seen: Painterly and realistic, with fur rendering and a clean outline. Not cel-shaded or cute in a toy way, though the face is soft and glider-like.

OURS.seen: Bespoke art, not a vanilla or other-mod animal.

ALPHA.seen: Clean cut-out on the checkerboard, with no shadow or ground.

SCALE.seen: A small tree-gliding animal about the human's height in wingspan. The description gives no size words that contradict this.

LEGIBLE.seen: At 32 px per cell it reads as a tan winged shape apart from the ground.
